steps.title: Everyday food
steps.body: Montepulciano d'Abruzzo is a classic pizza and pasta wine: its soft tannins and dark fruit suit tomato sauce, sausages and grilled meat. In Abruzzo, it goes with arrosticini, lamb skewers. Cerasuolo suits fish soups, charcuterie and summer food.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve at 16 to 18 degrees; Cerasuolo chilled at 10 to 12. Simple Montepulciano is best within three years. Colline Teramane and Conero Riserva age 10 to 15 years; some traditional producers' wines last decades.
steps.highlight: Simple wines young; the best for decades

steps.prompt: Which dish is a classic Abruzzo partner for Montepulciano?
steps.explanation: Grilled lamb skewers are Abruzzo's traditional match.

steps.body: An everyday Montepulciano d'Abruzzo is one of Italy's best-value reds for pizza night.

steps.prompt: Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo is best served chilled.
steps.explanation: Yes. As a rosé, it's served at 10 to 12 degrees.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Montepulciano suits pizza, pasta and grilled lamb
Serve reds at 16 to 18 degrees and Cerasuolo chilled
Top wines age 10 to 15 years or more
